To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the markets and prices of male goats of 1 2 years old and castrated goats of 4 years old are influenced by season of the year and that the majority of female goats purchased are for breeding and herd expansion.
the factors affecting goat prices are age, sex, season of sale and the market where the goats are sold.

the Rendille sell goats in the Ilaut market, the majority of sales being male goats of 1 2 years old, and castrates, and that the reasons for goat purchase are home and ceremonial slaughtering, and breeding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of goats among the pastoralists of northern Kenya.
the factors affecting markets for goats and their prices among the Rendilles pastoralists of Northern Kenyan.
the role that goats play in the lives of Rendille pastoral communities of Kenya and the factors that influence the markets and prices of the goats in these communities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

goats serve as important food and income sources to Rendille pastoralist and their markets are influenced by the seasons of the year, the age and sex classes of the goats, and the purpose of the sale.
the study revealed that the factors that affected the prices of goats among Rendille pastoralist were age and sex classes of the goats, season, markets and purpose of sale.
the Rendille people sell their goats in Ilaut market because it is a market for livestock, and it is the nearest market to their settlement and it is also termed "Nairobi one day".
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
goats are an important asset to the Rendille and they are sold in markets to generate income for food and non food items.
the Rendille people sell goats to generate income for their daily needs and also to buy food and other basic needs.
the factors affecting markets prices of goats among Rendille pastoralist are: seasonality, age, sex and the type of market.
The main takeaway from our work is that
goats are an important source of food and income for the Rendille community of Northern Kenya.
the Rendille are active participants in markets and that they sell their goats to cater for their needs and to earn cash.
the Rendille are able to sell and purchase goats in a market that is far from their homestead.
